title: literature/v1
description: nodes/<id>/literature/<timestamp>-<contributor>.yaml (D-3, D-25, D-32 v3.35): what the literature says of the statement. Any contributor may append one, unsigned, attributed by the service (D-23): a proposal, awaiting a steward or curator. A record signed by a steward of the target or by a curator (`via`, `key`, `signature`, as steward/v2) is a confirmation: it may name the proposal it confirms in `confirms`, or state the status itself. The gate refuses a signed record whose signer is neither; an unsigned record from anyone is accepted. The products publish the latest confirmed status as the node's `literature` and the latest uncovered proposal as `literature_proposed` (graph/v6, frontier/v5, context/v5). Earns nothing; changes no status; ranks nothing.

node.description: the node the record is filed under

contributor.description: the pseudonym or GitHub login that filed it; for a signed record, the signer's login

status.description: what the literature says of the statement (D-25 v3.35): `open`, no proof is known; `known`, a proof is published and not formalised; `elementary`, a routine formalisation of a known fact. A fact about the literature, never about difficulty.

references.description: what supports the status: a paper, a registry entry, a forum page; at least one, even for `open` (where the problem is listed)

url.description: rendered as a link only through the site's allowlist (F11-Q11)

note.description: what the reference establishes, in one sentence

summary.description: what is known, in the contributor's words; untrusted text, shown demarcated (D-31)

model_and_tooling.description: As declared by the operator (D-23); never verified

confirms.description: for a signed record: the proposal it confirms, relative to the node; null when the signer states the status themselves or when the record is a proposal

via.description: null for a proposal. For a confirmation, how the signature was made (D-3, D-32 v3.33): `ssh`, by the signer's own key; `approval-key`, by the network's approval key through the service for a login signed in on the site, in which case `key` must equal keys/approval.pub in the merge's parent tree.

key.description: null for a proposal; the key the signature verifies under

signature.description: null for a proposal; an OpenSSH SSHSIG armored signature over the record's canonical body (opn_gate.signed), made with the private half of `key`
